title: AI-Assisted Permit Intake and Review Automation Platform
summary: The City of Port Alder, Washington wants a cloud-hosted platform that helps people submit complete building and other permit applications the first time. AI would check each application for missing items, pull out key data, route it to the right reviewer and help (not replace) City plan reviewers. Today 41% of applications are sent back as incomplete and it takes a median 38 days to reach first review; the City wants to halve the returns and get first review under 15 days. The work includes an applicant portal, an English/Spanish assistant, a staff dashboard and two-way integration with the City's on-premises permitting system.

fit_factors.reason: An AI-assisted workflow-automation and compliance platform with a web portal is exactly what idiaz.io builds.
Remote work is allowed (only the kickoff is in person), but 24/7 Severity 1 on-call and a 9-month full release are heavy for a small team.
The Small Business set-aside likely favours us, but 3 years in business, two public-sector or regulated AI projects, WA registration and $2M cyber/E&O insurance all need checking.
The $420,000 cap must cover a large scope (PermitCore integration, 1.4 TB migration, 2 years of hosting), which squeezes margin.
The January 15, 2027 deadline gives about 7 weeks to write the proposal, but the pilot is due within 120 days of NTP.

reasons: Core match: an AI completeness-check and workflow-automation platform for a regulated permitting process is squarely idiaz.io's work.
Small Business set-aside, mostly remote delivery (only the PM's kickoff is in person) and US-only hosting suit a small US studio.
Clear success measures and UAT thresholds (90% completeness agreement, 95% routing accuracy) let a strong AI team stand out in scored demos.
change_mind: idiaz.io has been in business under 3 years, or cannot show two AI/automation projects for public-sector or regulated clients. Both are pass/fail minimums.
We cannot get $2M cyber and $2M professional liability insurance before contract execution.
A realistic estimate for the PermitCore SOAP/REST integration and 1.4 TB migration exceeds the $420,000 cap.
We cannot staff 24/7 Severity 1 on-call with a 4-hour resolution target.

open_questions: Is Year 3 subscription funded outside the $420,000 not-to-exceed amount, given the three-year term?
